title: MyLinden prescription terms: renewal lead time, reminders and the post-expiry window
content:
These terms apply to every prescription a patient holds on the Linden Ridge Prescriptions & Renewals line. They set, class by class, how far ahead of running out the patient is asked to request a renewal, how far ahead of the estimated run-out a refill reminder is sent, and how many calendar days after the expiration date an expired prescription may still be renewed.

| Class | Renewal requested ahead of running out (business days) | Refill reminder before the estimated run-out (days) | Post-expiry renewal window (calendar days after the expiration date) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acute Short-Course Prescription | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Standard Maintenance Prescription | 5 | 7 | 30 |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription | 5 | 7 | 14 |
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | 5 | 7 | 0 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 7 | 7 | 0 |
| Specialty Medication Prescription | 10 | 10 | 14 |

**Conditions.**

(a) A post-expiry renewal window of 0 means an expired prescription of that class cannot be renewed; a new prescription is needed. This is so for the Acute Short-Course Prescription and for both controlled classes.

(b) Where the window is above 0, it is the number of calendar days after the expiration date within which an expired prescription of that class may still be renewed.

(c) The lead time for requesting a renewal is counted in business days before the patient runs out; the reminder is counted in days before the estimated run-out date.

**Illustration (hypothetical).** For a Specialty Medication Prescription the patient is asked to request a renewal 10 business days before running out, a reminder is sent 10 days before the estimated run-out, and an expired prescription may still be renewed within 14 calendar days after its expiration date.
